Fanta was invented because Germany couldn't get Coca-Cola.
In 1940, during World War Two, the syrup for Coke couldn't reach the factories in Germany.
So the boss there, Max Keith, made a new drink from whatever was left.
Whey, the watery leftovers from making cheese. And apple pulp, the scraps from pressing cider.
He told his team to use their imagination, Fantasie in German.
It sold millions of bottles during the war.
The orange version didn't come until 1955, in Italy.
So next time you drink a Fanta, remember it started as cheese water and apple scraps.
